title: Ants: one frame, then the same slope stepping
question: Same 31 ants, same slope, same seed. In the single frame, can you find them at all? Then scrub the sequence. The measurement says the frozen frame has ~148 other things in it that look as much like an ant as an ant does, and the moving frames have 1 -- does that match what your eye does here?
context_md:
`creature-appearance-design.md` says extent is the only lever and has to roughly quadruple. That rests on `decoys` -- how many other places in the frame are as different from their surroundings as the animal is -- and it is computed on a **single still**, where a decoy is a rock edge or a leaf: something that holds still, while the animal does not.

Measured with the motion axis added: **a body that moves has 0-2 competitors at every size from 1 to 16 cells**, so a walking two-cell ant is already better off than a stationary sixteen-cell one. In every sky tested -- a storm moves 6,316 pixels and still produces none.

**The half that keeps it honest, and it is your own dead-ant observation as a number:** only 29% of these ants move in any given 8-frame gap and **42% never moved once across 384 frames**. For those, the still frame is the whole story.

Nothing on this branch changes a shipped creature.
